speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness over a year is highly suggestive of a cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy. Given your diabetes and hypertension, could you describe exactly where you feel the weakness in your hands, and do you have any numbness in your groin or saddle area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and progressive weakness alongside sensory symptoms in a 58-year-old male is highly characteristic of ALS. I am ready to finalize this assessment; do you have any difficulty with swallowing or breathing?
